title: A counterexample to the Eisenbud–Mazur conjecture
summary: We construct a height-five prime ideal $P$ in the six-variable formal power series ring $R$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ such that $P^{(2)}\not\subseteq\mathfrak{m}P$, thus providing a prime-ideal counterexample to the Eisenbud--Mazur conjecture (with $\mathbb{Q}$ being the coefficient field). The ideal is the kernel of an explicit quadratic parametrization over a number field of degree $28$ over $\mathbb{Q}$.
